MOSCOW, Oct 14 (Reuters) - A Russia-US [deal](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/what-is-diesel-deal-between-putin-trump-2026-10-12/) on supplies of Russian diesel can pave the way for further economic cooperation between the ​two countries, Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said on Wednesday, adding ‌that Moscow would overcome any sanctions-related difficulties to ensure the fuel was delivered.

US President [Donald Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/donald-trump/) said last Friday that he and Russian counterpart [Vladimir Putin](https://www.reuters.com/topic/person/vladimir-putin/) had [reached an agreement](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/trump-big-announcement-coming-up-diesel-2026-10-09/) ​for Russia to release supplies of diesel to the US ​and global markets.

Trump is keen to lower US diesel prices ⁠ahead of November 3 US mid-term elections.

The deal, which required Trump to ​lift some US sanctions that he himself had imposed against Russia, was ​strongly criticised by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and European officials.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev attends a meeting of Russian President Vladimir Putin with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, at the Kremlin in Moscow, Russia, September 5, 2026. Dmitriev said the deal could serve as a model for further ones, and that Russia intended to continue its ​economic engagement with the US.

"It's not just about the diesel deal; ​there are many other opportunities for economic and investment cooperation with the US that ‌benefit ⁠Russia, the United States, and global markets alike," he told reporters.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

The Kremlin has repeatedly said it sees potential for profitable cooperation with the United States across a range of economic areas including energy and minerals, expressing ​regret that Washington ​has previously made ⁠such deals conditional on ending the war in Ukraine.

Dmitriev said Russia would continue to engage with the US ​on economic and investment projects and "keep explaining, using concrete ​examples, ⁠that American sanctions primarily hurt the American people and American farmers".

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Wednesday that the diesel deal was a ["very risky ⁠choice"](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-russia-deal-diesel-is-very-risky-choice-italy-pm-meloni-says-2026-10-14/) ​that ran counter to efforts to force Putin ​to sit down and negotiate a peace deal with [Ukraine](https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraine-russia-war/).
